http.hero.title: HTTP Event Push API
http.hero.subtitle: After a third-party HTTP URL is configured on the platform, the platform pushes algorithm events to the third-party system.
http.basic.requestUrl.desc: The URL configured by the user on the platform page
http.basic.successCriteria.desc: HTTP status code 200, and the response body should be valid JSON, e.g. {"resCode":1}.
http.basic.note: When pushing over HTTP, picture fields are converted to base64 strings; the video field is a local file path on the platform. The video file may still be being written when the event is produced, so third-party systems are advised to wait a few seconds before reading it.
http.field.messageId.desc: Unique event ID, used for link tracing and retry de-duplication.
http.field.algorithmCode.desc: Algorithm code. In the current implementation it is usually the same as algorithmId.
http.field.areaId.desc: Area ID where the event occurred.
http.field.areaName.desc: Area name where the event occurred.
http.field.orignalPicture.desc: Original full picture. The field name keeps the historical spelling orignalPicture for compatibility.
http.field.detectedPicture.desc: Detected target thumbnail, may be empty.
http.field.video.desc: Alarm video path, may be empty.
http.field.videostructured.desc: Path of the structured target/area info file for the video, may be empty.
http.field.overviewFile.desc: Path of the event process overview file, may be empty.
http.field.recordId.desc: Target or alarm record ID. With tracking enabled it usually stays the same for one target.
http.field.isRetryMessage.desc: Whether this is an offline retry message.
http.field.property.desc: Algorithm extension properties. Only present when the corresponding algorithm has extension properties.
http.propertyRules.desc: property outputs the sub-object matching the algorithm type; not all sub-objects appear at the same time.
http.sub.peopleCounting: People Count, Vehicle Flow, Single-frame Count & Crowd
http.passflowPush.desc: Passenger flow algorithms (e.g. 67954) push only on line crossing instead of on the people-count report interval. A POST is made only when at least one of enterOrgNum/leaveOrgNum is non-zero. The push carries the OSD snapshot of the crossing moment (with enter/leave text and tripwire overlaid) as JPEG base64; all three pictures are the same frame. On failure the event joins the 24-hour offline retry like other events. Configure the push URL and select algorithms under Data Docking.
http.passflow.field.enterOrgNum.desc: Increment of this crossing. 1 means one person just entered.
http.passflow.field.enterNumber.desc: Cumulative enters in the current hour.
http.passflow.field.leaveNumber.desc: Cumulative leaves in the current hour.
http.osdSnapshot.desc: Third-party systems pull the current channel picture (with detection boxes, tripwires and enter/leave counts) using the snapshot key (apiKey). Do not use the web admin account. The system has only one admin; third-party requests only carry the apiKey header — ask the device administrator for it. The key is not the same as the admin password.
http.osdSnapshot.snapshotNote: Pass base64:"0" to get only the URL. Open fullUrl with GET to get the JPEG file directly.
http.osd.field.algorithmId.desc: Algorithm ID; pick an entry with enableStatus=1.
http.osd.field.base64.desc: Optional. By default the response includes pictureBase64 (JPEG base64); pass \"0\" to get only url/fullUrl without base64.
